build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

comments.text: Death program: one page from track 4, logical sector 2 of side 1, the end of the game. The game's main loop ($7ED5-$7EFC) tests the character records 1 to $0A (records_in_use): one that is conscious (CON 1 or more), or only unconscious (condition UNC, CON -1 to -10) with no disease bits (+$28 = 0), counts as alive. When none does, or $0A is 0, it asks for side 1 (check_side_1 $02D5) and loads this sector with load_program ($03AD, $10 = 4, $11 = 2) over the game's own first page; load_program reads the header at death_header and jumps here. This JMP steps over the header to death_main.
Program header read by load_program ($2890): +3/+4 the load address $7E00, +5 the page count 1. The JMP at $7E00 steps over it.

Shows the end of the game and stops there. Copies the 12 bytes of death_caption ("Grim Reaper ", not the zero after them) over the location name at $F4D0 (the byte after them, $F4DC, is 0 in both death snapshots, so the name ends there); shows picture $3B from the buffer at $E000 (show_picture_e000 $041C, which frames the picture window and prints that name under it); redraws the roster (roster_show $02B7); opens the text window (text_window_open $0353) and prints death_text word-wrapped (print_string_wrapped $026F with $31/$32 = $7E3C). Then it reads keys for ever (wait_key $022F and JMP back, death_wait_forever): every key is taken and ignored, and RESTORE does nothing either (the NMI vector leads to an RTI, $04F6 to $2966), so only a reset leaves this screen. Nothing here writes to the disk, so the last saved game stays as it was.

Low byte ($2F) of the operand of LDA $7E2F,X at $7E08, inside death_main. The automatic symbol comes from the game's LDA $7E09,Y at $A1D5 and INC $7E09,X at $A6E7, which address a table in the game's own page $7E00; this program has replaced that page, and that game code never runs again once it is loaded.

Low byte ($D0) of the operand of STA $F4D0,X at $7E0B, inside death_main. The symbol comes from the game's LDA $7E0C,Y ($A15E, $A695) and STA $7E0C,Y ($A6AC), written for a table of the game's own page $7E00 (hit_list_damage), which this program has replaced.

High byte ($F4) of the operand of STA $F4D0,X at $7E0B, inside death_main. The symbol comes from the game's LDA $7E0D,Y ($A165, $A69D), ORA $7E0D,Y ($A16C) and STA $7E0D,Y ($A6A8), another table of the game's own page $7E00, gone while this program is loaded.

Offset ($F5) of the BNE at $7E11 that loops the caption copy back to $7E08. The symbol comes from the game's LDA $7E12,Y ($A251) and INC $7E12,X ($A659), which address its own page $7E00, not this program.

Caption for the picture window: "Grim Reaper " in ASCII, the order of the game's font (glyph c at $C600 + (c - $20) * 8), 12 bytes ($7E2F-$7E3A), then a zero at $7E3B that the copy loop in death_main does not take.

Second byte of death_caption, the "r" of "Grim". Its automatic symbol comes from the game's STA $7E30,Y ($9FC3), LDA $7E30,Y ($A1EA), and AND and STA $7E30,X ($A726, $A729), accesses to the game's own page $7E00 that do not apply to this program.
Fifth byte of death_caption, the space after "Grim". Its automatic symbol comes from the game's LDA $7E33,Y ($A1F6) and STA $7E33,X ($A72E), meant for the game's own page $7E00, not this caption.

The message of the death screen, in ASCII: "Your life has ended in The Wasteland...", RETURN ($0D at $7E63, a new line) and a zero ($7E64). death_main prints it word-wrapped in the text window. (The automatic symbol at $7E63 is the target of the game's BEQ at $7E5E and JMP $7E63 at $7F14, its own main loop, which this program has replaced.)

The 155 bytes after death_text are never read by this program: an exact copy of bytes $65-$FF of track 4, logical sector 1, the first page of the logo font that the start-up reads to $CA00-$CBFF ($7FA4; play-title.vsf holds it there). Stale contents of the sector, not part of the death screen.

Byte $19 of death_leftover. The automatic symbol comes from the engine's menu call (the JSR at $1C71), whose operand still held $7E7E, the Ranger Center's Start handler, when the snapshot was taken; the death program never calls menu_key ($02DE), so nothing jumps here.
